questions.question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

The last time he repeated / the same mistake I thought he would / feel many sorry but I was wrong.

options.text: feel many sorry but I was wrong.
the same mistake I thought he would

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 2' **i.e. **"feel many sorry but I was wrong."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The** error** in this segment lies in the use of the phrase **"feel many sorry,"** which is grammatically incorrect.
 
• The** correct phrase **should be **"feel very sorry" or "feel so sorry."**
 
• In English, we** do not use ***"many"* in conjunction **with ***"sorry".*
 
• **"Many"** is used with countable nouns to indicate a large number, while "sorry" is an adjective and doesn't have a plural form, thus it cannot be counted.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *"The last time he repeated the same mistake I thought he would feel very sorry, but I was wrong."*

• The sentence* "I rode my bike to 'worked those' morning"* is grammatically incorrect.

• **"work these"** - This option is incorrect. The word "these" is a plural demonstrative pronoun and doesn't fit in this context. We're referring to a single, specific morning (the one today), so we should use "this."

The timescale of prokaryote evolution / have been difficult to reconstruct / because of a limited fossil record.

options.text: because of a limited fossil record.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 3' **i.e. **"have been difficult to reconstruct".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** error in** this segment is a **subject-verb agreement **problem.
 
• **The subject** *"The timescale of prokaryote evolution"* is singular.
 
• Therefore, the verb should also be singular to match.
 
• The** correct verb **form in this context is** "has," not "have."**

Therefore, the** correct sentence** is: *"The timescale of prokaryote evolution** has been** difficult to reconstruct because of a limited fossil record."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Here's the explanation for each segment:
 
 
• **"because of a limited fossil record" -** This segment is grammatically correct. It serves as an explanation for why the reconstruction has been difficult.
 
• **"The timescale of prokaryote evolution" **- This segment is also grammatically correct. It is a noun phrase that serves as the subject of the sentence.

• **The sentence** suggests that by joining the networks, one can help to improve or enhance (i.e., "promote") better Governance.
 
• The term** "Governance"** usually refers to the processes of interaction and decision-making among the actors involved in a collective problem.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *'Join our networks to promote better Governance.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **"Drain"** - This verb generally means to cause the water or other liquid in something to run out, leaving it empty, dry, or drier. In a metaphorical sense, it can mean to exhaust or deplete resources, which is not a positive or appropriate action for improving Governance.
 
• **"Disintegrate"** - This verb means to break up into small parts or to cause something to do this, usually as a result of impact or decay. It implies destruction or the breaking down of something, which does not align with the goal of bettering Governance.
 
• **"Sedate" **- This verb means to administer a sedative to someone or to calm them down. In a metaphorical sense, it could imply pacifying or suppressing activity. It doesn't make sense in this context because it doesn't suggest any action that would improve Governance.

• A multi-client messaging system facilitates communication among various users, making it easier for them to stay connected, hence "keep in touch."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.**

I ______ the cake before my mother arrived.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 1' **i.e. **"had baked."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In this sentence, two past events are mentioned: baking the cake and mother's arrival.
 
• When** two actions occur **in the** past,** the action that happened first is usually in the past perfect tense, while the action that happened second is in the simple past tense.
 
• In this sentence, *"before my mother arrived"* is in the **simple past**, so the baking of the cake, which happened first, should be in the past perfect ("had baked").

Therefore, the **correct sentence **is:* 'I** had baked ** the cake before my mother arrived.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Here's the explanation for each option:
 
 
• **"Bake" -** This is the base form of the verb, typically used in the present tense. It is not suitable for this sentence, which refers to past actions.
 
• **"Baked" -** This is the past simple form of the verb. It can be used to indicate a completed action in the past, but when describing two events that both occurred in the past, the action that happened first (baking the cake) should be in the past perfect tense.
 
• **"Have baked" -** This is the present perfect form of the verb. It's used to connect the past and the present, often to describe an action that happened in the past but is still relevant in the present. It does not fit in this sentence, which refers to two distinct past events.

Eventually, the water will ______ through the surrounding concrete.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **"Delegate"** - This verb typically means to entrust a task or responsibility to another person, typically one who is less senior than oneself. It is not relevant in the context of water and concrete.
